19179-kelly-miller-s-history-of-the-worl.title: Pictures of the Negro in Action in Both Army and Navy.
19179-kelly-miller-s-history-of-the-worl.creator: Unknown
19179-kelly-miller-s-history-of-the-worl.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. In this treatise, Professor Miller will trace briefly, but with consuming interest, the relation of the Negro to the great wars of the past. He will point out the never-failing fount of loyalty and patriotism which characterizes the black man's nature, and will show that the Negro has never been a hireling, but has always been characterized by that moral energy which actuates all true heroism.

arxiv-2012-08368.title: E. Di Salvo
arxiv-2012-08368.creator: a,b,
arxiv-2012-08368.description:
A 2020 arXiv research paper by a,b,. Parametrizations of the Spin Density Matrix

Abstract

We propose for the spin density matrix two parametrizations which automatically fulfil the non-negativity conditions, without setting any bound on the parameters. The first one relies on a theorem, that we prove, and it is rather simple and easily adaptable to some specific reactions, where, for example, parity is conserved or angular momentum conservation entails selection rules.

arxiv-2105-08219.title: A time-domain nearfield frequency-invariant beamforming method Thanks: This work is sponsored by the Australian Research Council (ARC) Discovery Projects funding schemes with project numbers DP200100693. Thanks: Fei Ma, Thushara D. Abhayapala, and Prasanga N. Samarasinghe are all with the Research S
arxiv-2105-08219.creator: Fei Ma, Thushara D. Abhayapala
arxiv-2105-08219.description: Abstract Most existing beamforming methods are frequency-domain methods, and are designed for enhancing a farfield target source over a narrow frequency band. They have found diverse applications and are still under active development. However, they struggle to achieve desired performance if the target source is in the nearfield with a broadband output.

arxiv-2105-13718.title: Voice Activity Detection for Ultrasound-based Silent Speech Interfaces using Convolutional Neural Networks
arxiv-2105-13718.creator: Amin Honarmandi Shandiz, László Tóth
arxiv-2105-13718.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Amin Honarmandi Shandiz, László Tóth. Voice Activity Detection (VAD) is not easy task when the input audio signal is noisy, and it is even more complicated when the input is not even an audio recording. This is the case with Silent Speech Interfaces (SSI) where we record the movement of the articulatory organs during speech, and we aim to reconstruct the speech signal from this recording.

arxiv-2201-13201.title: The Donor of the Black-Hole X-Ray Binary MAXI J1820+070
arxiv-2201-13201.creator: Joanna Mikołajewska, Andrzej A. Zdziarski, Janusz Ziółkowski, Manuel A. P. Torres, Jorge Casares
arxiv-2201-13201.description: Abstract We estimate the parameters of the donor of the accreting black-hole binary MAXI J1820+070. The measured values of the binary period, rotational and radial velocities and constraints on the orbital inclination imply the donor is a subgiant with the mass of M 2 ≈ 0.49 − 0.10 + 0.10 ​ M ☉ M_{2}\approx 0.49^{+0.10}_{-0.

arxiv-2311-15843.title: Robustness-Guaranteed Observer-Based Control Strategy with Modularity for Cleantech EMLA-Driven Heavy-Duty Robotic Manipulator
arxiv-2311-15843.creator: Mehdi Heydari Shahna, Mohammad Bahari, Jouni Mattila
arxiv-2311-15843.description: Abstract This paper introduces an innovative observer-based modular control strategy in a class of n a n_{a} -degree-of-freedom (DoF) fully electrified heavy-duty robotic manipulators (HDRMs) to (1) guarantee robustness in the presence of uncertainties and disturbances, (2) address the complexities arising from several interacting mechanisms, (3) ensure uniformly exponential stability, and (4) enhance overall control performance.

arxiv-2505-19198.title: New Results On S − r − S-r- ideals in Commutative Rings
arxiv-2505-19198.creator: Abuzer Gündüz, Osama A. Naji, Mehmet Özen
arxiv-2505-19198.description: Abstract . This article studies the notion of S − r − S-r- ideals in commutative ring H H , where S S is a multiplicatively closed subset of H H . Some basic properties of S − r − S-r- ideals are given. Various characterizations of S − r − S-r- ideals are presented.

arxiv-2507-20765.title: Onboard Hyperspectral Super-Resolution with Deep Pushbroom Neural Network
arxiv-2507-20765.creator: Davide Piccinini, Diego Valsesia, and Enrico Magli
arxiv-2507-20765.description: Abstract Hyperspectral imagers on satellites obtain the fine spectral signatures essential for distinguishing one material from another at the expense of limited spatial resolution. Enhancing the latter is thus a desirable preprocessing step in order to further improve the detection capabilities offered by hyperspectral images on downstream tasks.

arxiv-2508-20159.title: Nonlinear Hall effect in topological Dirac semimetals in parallel magnetic field
arxiv-2508-20159.creator: Maxim Dzero, Maxim Khodas, Alex Levchenko, Vladyslav Kozii
arxiv-2508-20159.description: Abstract We compute the second-harmonic response of two-dimensional topological Dirac semimetals subjected to an in-plane magnetic field. The quantum kinetic equation for the Wigner distribution function is derived and then solved to compute the second-order electric-field contributions to the current density.

arxiv-2601-19513.title: Enhancing Academic Paper Recommendations Using Fine-Grained Knowledge Entities and Multifaceted Document Embeddings
arxiv-2601-19513.creator: Haixu Xi, Heng Zhang, Chengzhi Zhang
arxiv-2601-19513.description: Abstract In the era of explosive growth in academic literature, the burden of literature review on scholars are increasing. Proactively recommending academic papers that align with scholars’ literature needs in the research process has become one of the crucial pathways to enhance research efficiency and stimulate innovative thinking.

pmc-10619101.title: MyCOACH (COnnected Advice for Cognitive Health): a digitally delivered multidomain intervention for cognitive decline and risk of dementia in adults with mild cognitive impairment or subjective cognitive decline–study protocol for a randomised controlled trial
pmc-10619101.creator: Jessica G Amos, Lidan Zheng, Ranmalee Eramudugolla, Dinaz Parekh, Md Hamidul Huque, Kim Delbaere, Nicola Lautenschlager, Kaarin J Anstey
pmc-10619101.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). pmc-11336203.title: Association mapping and candidate gene identification for yield traits in European hazelnut ( Corylus avellana L.)
pmc-11336203.creator: Asena Akköse Baytar, Ertuğrul Gazi Yanar, Anne Frary, Sami Doğanlar
pmc-11336203.description: European hazelnut ( Corylus avellana L.) is an important nut crop due to its nutritional benefits, culinary uses, and economic value. Türkiye is the leading producer of hazelnut, followed by Italy and the United States. Quantitative trait locus studies offer promising opportunities for breeders and geneticists to identify genomic regions controlling desirable traits in hazelnut.

pmc-11356717.title: Response Surface Methodology-Based Optimization of the Chitinolytic Activity of Burkholderia contaminans Strain 614 Exerting Biological Control against Phytopathogenic Fungi
pmc-11356717.creator: Imen Ben Slimene Debez, Hayet Houmani, Henda Mahmoudi, Khaoula Mkadmini, Pedro Garcia-Caparros, Ahmed Debez, Olfa Tabbene, Naceur Djébali, Maria-Camino Urdaci
pmc-11356717.description: As part of the development of alternative and environmentally friendly control against phytopathogenic fungi, Burkholderia cepacia could be a useful species notably via the generation of hydrolytic enzymes like chitinases, which can act as a biological control agent. Here, a Burkholderia contaminans S614 strain exhibiting chitinase activity was isolated from a soil in southern Tunisia.

pmc-11359503.title: U-TAG: Electromagnetic Wireless Sensing System for Robotic Hand Pre-Grasping
pmc-11359503.creator: Armin Gharibi, Filippo Costa, Simone Genovesi, Anastasios Doulamis, Francesco Della Corte
pmc-11359503.description: In order to perform complex manipulation and grasp tasks, robotic hands require sensors that can handle increasingly demanding functionality and degrees of freedom. This research paper proposes a radiofrequency sensor that uses a wireless connection between a probe and a tag.

pmc-11516823.title: Monitoring the level of health and inequality over time using the Population Health Performance Index
pmc-11516823.creator: A Grün, K Bozorgmehr, A Nowak
pmc-11516823.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). BackgroundThe Population Health Performance Index (PHPI) is a composite measure that combines average health outcomes and their distribution within a population, thereby allowing for a comprehensive assessment of population health and inequality.

pmc-11578373.title: Tumor Microenvironment Activated Cu Crosslinked Near‐Infrared Sonosensitizers for Visualized Cuproptosis‐Enhanced Sonodynamic Cancer Immunotherapy
pmc-11578373.creator: Jinyan Hu, Lang Yan, Zhi Cao, Bijiang Geng, Xiqian Cao, Bing Liu, Jiaming Guo, Jiangbo Zhu
pmc-11578373.description: Reactive oxygen species (ROS)‐mediated sonodynamic therapy (SDT) holds increasing potential in treating deep‐seated tumor owing to the high tissue‐penetration depth. However, the inevitable accumulation of sonosensitizers in normal tissues not only make it difficult to realize the in situ SDT, but also induces sonodynamic effects in normal tissues.

pmc-11634475.title: Improved health by combining dietary restriction and promoting muscle growth in DNA repair‐deficient progeroid mice
pmc-11634475.creator: Wilbert P. Vermeij, Khalid Alyodawi, Ivar van Galen, Jennie L. von der Heide, María B. Birkisdóttir, Lisanne J. van't Sant, Rutger A. Ozinga, Daphne S.J. Komninos, Kimberly Smit, Yvonne M.A. Rijksen, Renata M.C. Brandt, Sander Barnhoorn, Dick Jaarsma, Sathivel Vaiyapuri, Olli Ritvos, Tobias B. Huber
pmc-11634475.description: BackgroundAgeing is a complex multifactorial process, impacting all organs and tissues, with DNA damage accumulation serving as a common underlying cause. To decelerate ageing, various strategies have been applied to model organisms and evaluated for health and lifespan benefits. Dietary restriction (DR, also known as caloric restriction) is a well‐established long‐term intervention recognized for its universal anti‐ageing effects.

pmc-11727177.title: Exploring the Complex Relationship Between Antidepressants, Depression and Neurocognitive Disorders
pmc-11727177.creator: Monica Neațu, Iulia Ioniță, Ana Jugurt, Eugenia Irene Davidescu, Bogdan Ovidiu Popescu, Giovanni Lentini, Serge Mignani
pmc-11727177.description: The coexistence of dementia and depression in older populations presents a complex clinical challenge, with each condition often exacerbating the other. Cognitive decline can intensify mood disturbances, and untreated or recurring depression accelerates neurodegenerative processes. As depression is a recognized risk factor for dementia, it is crucial to address both conditions concurrently to prevent further deterioration.

pmc-12433152.title: See more, do less?—resident-reported training trends in reconstructive urology
pmc-12433152.creator: Kevin Neuzil, Eric Wallen, John R. Potts, Molly E. DeWitt-Foy
pmc-12433152.description: BackgroundUrologic surgical training has been dramatically affected by numerous practice changes including a significant increase in robotic surgery, rise of subspecialty fellows, and even the coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) pandemic, among others. How resident training has been affected is not well understood.

pmc-12862198.title: “Doing the Best I Can”: Qualitative Outcomes and Participant Feedback From a Combined Communication and Counselling Treatment for Primary Progressive Aphasia
pmc-12862198.creator: Kristin Schaffer Mendez, William S. Evans, Christina D. Dutcher, Christina Philburn, Lisa D. Wauters, Megan M. Young, Maya L. Henry
pmc-12862198.description: IntroductionThere is a growing evidence base supporting the utility of restitutive speech‐language treatments for individuals with primary progressive aphasia (PPA). In contrast, there is limited research investigating treatment approaches that offer counselling to this population. Given that people with PPA are susceptible to negative impacts on their psychosocial well‐being, research is needed to address this underrepresented area of inquiry.

pmc-12980188.title: Nucleoside Analogue with Thymidine Nucleobase Inhibits Leishmania infantum and Depolarizes the Plasma Membrane Potential In Vitro
pmc-12980188.creator: Clarissa Menezes, Ingrid de O. Dias, Elisa Pileggi, Andre G. Tempone, Fabrizio Pertusati, Samanta E. T. Borborema
pmc-12980188.description: Visceral leishmaniasis, caused by the protozoan parasites Leishmania infantum or L. donovani, remains a lethal neglected tropical disease without effective therapy. Current drugs available are toxic, leading to severe side effects, treatment abandonment, and resistance, underscoring the urgent need for new therapeutic options. As Leishmania spp.

pmc-13258505.title: Effect of Sb on the Hot Ductility and Fracture Behavior of Low-Alloy Corrosion-Resistant Steel
pmc-13258505.creator: Zhiwei Liu, Wang Li, Xiuhua Gao, Linxiu Du, Hongyan Wu, Ruiqi Zhang
pmc-13258505.description: The mechanism by which Sb influences the hot ductility and fracture behavior of corrosion-resistant steel within the temperature range of 650–1200 °C was systematically investigated using scanning electron microscopy (SEM) and electron probe microanalysis (EPMA). The temperature interval of the ductility trough and the underlying mechanisms responsible for its occurrence were elucidated.

pmc-13495980.title: Techniques and challenges in studying photosynthetic diversity in freshwater submerged vascular plants
pmc-13495980.creator: Ellie Loew‐Mendelson, David Wickell, Calista Mrozinski, Lizzy Iliana Doan, Jason Hupp, Richard L. Vath, Lingling Yuan, Karolina Heyduk
pmc-13495980.description: While the photosynthetic diversity of aquatic plants rivals that of terrestrial species, the environmental conditions underlying that diversity fundamentally differ. Despite these environmental differences, aquatic and terrestrial plants have convergently evolved carbon concentrating mechanisms (CCMs). However, characterization of these pathways in submerged plants has lagged behind terrestrial systems due to methodological constraints of the aquatic environment.

pmc-13509546.title: Clinical and Epidemiological Landscape of Antimicrobial Resistance and Virulence in Streptococcus Species
pmc-13509546.creator: Telma de Sousa, Catarina Silva, José Eduardo Pereira, Gilberto Igrejas, Patricia Poeta
pmc-13509546.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Species of the genus Streptococcus constitute important pathogens in human and veterinary medicine, being responsible for a wide spectrum of infections ranging from mild illnesses to severe invasive pathologies. Although β-lactams continue to be effective against most species, the global increase in resistance to macrolides, lincosamides, tetracyclines, and, in some cases, reduced susceptibility to penicillin represents a growing challenge for antimicrobial therapy.

pmc-13563533.title: Sources of the N15 TMS-evoked potential following motor cortex stimulation localize rostrals to TMS-induced electric fields and depend on dose
pmc-13563533.creator: Sybren Van Hoornweder, Mikkel M Beck, Jesper D Nielsen, Leo Tomasevic, Raf LJ Meesen, Hartwig R Siebner, Axel Thielscher
pmc-13563533.description: Transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS) elicits characteristic cortical responses known as TMS-evoked potentials (TEPs) measured via electroencephalography (EEG). An early negative peak can be consistently evoked over the motor cortex at around 15 ms (N15). It remains elusive whether N15 overlaps with the cortical regions receiving the highest TMS-induced electric field (E-field).
